questions.stem: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was a victory of the English East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal. Who led the English forces?
questions.explanation: Plassey, 23 June 1757 — Robert Clive with ~3,000 troops defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah's ~50,000 after the secret defection of Mir Jafar, Siraj's own commander. Mir Jafar was installed as a puppet Nawab. Hector Munro led the British at Buxar (1764); Warren Hastings was later Governor-General (1772-85); Cornwallis came in 1786.

questions.stem: At the Battle of Buxar (1764), the British defeated a combined army of three leaders. Which of the following was NOT part of that alliance?

options.option_text: Shah Alam II, the Mughal emperor

questions.explanation: Buxar — 22 October 1764 — Hector Munro defeated the triple alliance of Mir Qasim (deposed Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Haider Ali of Mysore fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore Wars, not at Buxar. The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) handed the British the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

questions.stem: Match the battle with its year. A. First Battle of Panipat. B. Second Battle of Panipat. C. Third Battle of Panipat. D. Battle of Plassey. List-II: 1. 1526, 2. 1556, 3. 1761, 4. 1757.
questions.explanation: Panipat I (1526): Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi — the Mughal empire begins. Panipat II (1556): Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan vs Hemu. Panipat III (1761): Ahmad Shah Abdali vs the Marathas (Sadashivrao Bhau) — catastrophic Maratha defeat. Plassey (1757): Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.stem: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) effectively ended the colonial ambitions in India of which European power?
questions.explanation: Wandiwash, 22 January 1760, during the Third Carnatic War — Sir Eyre Coote (English EIC) decisively defeated Comte de Lally (French). French military power in India was finished; only Puducherry and Mahé survived as French enclaves until their peaceful handover in 1954. The Portuguese held Goa till 1961; Dutch and Danish presence had already faded earlier in the 18th century.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', was killed while defending which fort against the British?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan fell on 4 May 1799 defending Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) against Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington) in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. Tipu pioneered iron-cased rocket artillery that later inspired the British Congreve rocket. After his death, the British restored the Wadiyar dynasty as a subordinate ally.

questions.stem: The Kargil War between India and Pakistan took place in which year?
questions.explanation: Kargil, May-July 1999 — the Indian Army's Operation Vijay and the IAF's Operation Safed Sagar evicted Pakistani intruders from heights in the Kargil-Dras sector along the LoC. Atal Bihari Vajpayee was PM. 26 July is observed as Kargil Vijay Diwas. 1965 and 1971 were earlier Indo-Pak wars.

questions.stem: The 1971 Indo-Pak war led to the creation of which new nation?
questions.explanation: The 1971 war (3-16 December) was triggered by the Bangladesh Liberation movement in East Pakistan. India's intervention ended in Pakistan's surrender at Dhaka on 16 December 1971 — Lt Gen A.A.K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender before Lt Gen Jagjit Singh Aurora; around 93,000 Pakistani soldiers became prisoners of war. 16 December is observed as Vijay Diwas. Myanmar (then Burma), Sri Lanka (Ceylon) and Bhutan already existed as separate states in 1971.
